rationale: Reduplicated verb of mingling appearing four times on this page (lines 6, 16, 20, 24) in the cosmic non-interference context. Related to ⲗⲱⲃϣ 'mingle' (in glossary). The Wheel and heavens 'do not mingle' = do not physically interpenetrate. Distinct from ⲡⲱⲍ/ⲡⲱⲣⲭ 'cleave/separate.'

Lycopolitan ⲕⲟⲟⲍ likely = ⲕⲟⲟϩ 'corner, edge, prominence.' In the ship-simile context (lines 11-17) functions as the projecting prow-piece (often a lion-figure on ancient ships) which cleaves through waves. Paired with ⲧⲁⲡ 'head' to specify location at the ship's foremost head.
Lycopolitan particle/formation introducing direct discourse: 'questioned him, ⲡⲓⲫⲉ "Indeed, our Lord..."' Possibly related to ⲡⲉϫⲉ-/ⲡⲉϫⲁ⸗ 'said.' Confidence low; flagged for parallel attestation.

While glossary lists ⲡⲧⲭⲁⲓ̈ as 'the abode (tentative),' on this page (lines 12, 14, 16, 17) the term clearly designates a ship in a maritime simile (figurehead at prow, path through waves). Likely cognate with ϫⲁⲓ̈ 'ship.' The ship-meaning should be added as an attested sense alongside 'abode.'
Lycopolitan ⲡⲧⲁⲡ likely = ⲧⲁⲡ 'head, horn, tip' with prosthetic ⲡⲧ-. Used here architecturally for the topmost head of the ship (= prow). Distinguished from ⲁⲡⲉ/ⲁⲁⲡⲉ 'head' in earlier vocabulary.
Lycopolitan qualitative possibly from ⲥⲱϩⲉ 'stand, set' or ⲥⲁϩⲉ 'establish.' Used of the figurehead 'which is stationed at the head from the front of the ship.' Static-locative qualitative.

Possibly habitual auxiliary ϣⲁⲩ- with ⲕⲱⲛ-element, or a discourse-marker. Functions in line 11 to introduce a customary/typical comparison. Etymology unclear; confidence low. Flagged for parallel attestation.

Variant spelling/form possibly = ⲡⲏⲩⲉ 'heavens' with prosthetic ⲙ̄ⲡ-, or plural of ⲡⲧⲏⲩ 'wind.' In line 5 the heavens are 'stretched from the X to the earth' — context allows either reading. Tentatively 'winds' but 'heavens' also possible.
